title: Sofoco
author: Laura Ortiz Gómez
description: En «Sofoco», los personajes respiran aires de anhelo y amenaza. Estos nueve cuentos recorren paisajes en los que el imaginario popular se encuentra con la expresión literaria. title: Las aventuras de la China Iron
author: Gabriela Cabezón Cámara
description: Radiante, luminoso. El desierto es un prisma de perros, cardos, polvo y cielo. La China Iron acompaña a Liz, una inglesa que va tras su marido llevado por la leva. Ella, en cambio, no busca a Martín Fierro, ese gaucho que se la ganó en un partido de truco. La China escapa. Y es su viaje exploración: de la textura de la seda, del sabor del té, del sofoco en que estalla el sexo. Descubre palabras. Sonidos nuevos para cosas que antes no existían. Pasan del desierto al fortín, un experimento social que intenta transformar a una masa de criollos brutos en los ciudadanos industriosos que pide la Nación.

title: Exit Reality
author: Valentina Tanni
description: Un recorrido por las estéticas de internet que imaginan espacios más allá de lo real: vaporwave, backrooms, weirdcore y otros paisajes liminales. Edición en inglés del original italiano de 2023, publicada por Nero junto con Aksioma.

entries.text: . It seems to be coming from some far-off place, but is actually from a distant time.
an unfulfilled promise

Wikipedia calls vaporwave a “subculture” and an “internet meme” that is a “microgenre of electronic music” and a recognizable “visual style,” characterized by a “nostalgic or surrealist engagement with the popular entertainment, technology and advertising of previous decades
Vaporwave is the first musical genre born and raised on the internet
Global capitalism is nearly there. At the end of the world there will only be liquid advertisement and gaseous desire

senses will endlessly ride escalators through pristine artificial environments, more and less than human, drugged-up and drugged down, catalysed, consuming and consumed by a relentlessly rich economy of sensory information, valued by the pixel

accelerationism is “the notion that the dissolution of civilisation wrought by capitalism should not and cannot be resisted, but rather must be pushed faster and farther towards the insanity and anarchically fluid violence that is its ultimate conclusion, either because this is liberating, because it causes a revolution, or because destruction is the only logical answer
virtual plaza” is the digital equivalent of the social spaces we frequent in the offline world: squares, parks, shopping malls.
when the internet represented a future full of opportunities, creativity, and social interaction

Nostalgia for the internet of the past, archaic technological products turned into surreal icons, a “solid” reality that “dissolves” into an intricate labyrinth of fleeting impressions and dreamy atmospheres, broken promises and clouds of vapor, a mixture of sarcasm and genuine affection for the fetish objects of techno-capitalism, clouds, and digital haze
the mother aesthetic, which all the others, in one way or another, have sprung from

a form of psychedelia” whose imagery comes not from the 1960s of LSD and the Summer of Love, but rather the hyper-consumerist 1980s of MTV, video games, and new consumer electronics, preferably Japanese (Sony, Panasonic, Toshiba, Fuji, etc.)
an unconscious expression of a kind of collective memory: “pop music refracted through the memory of a memory
Far Side Virtual: conceived as a collection of cell phone ringtones, the album pioneered a “hyperrealist” muzak explicitly intended to invoke the cool yet kitschy aesthetics of hi-tech consumerism
the archaeology of the recent past

Relive the memories. Reliving memories. The ghosts of memories, the “memories of memories” activated by hypnagogic pop, the “archaeology of the recent past” developed by artists like Ferraro and Lopatin: these are the cornerstones of the entire vaporwave
the specter of nostalgia
hauntology as a kind of nostalgia for past, lost, unrealized futures
“In conditions of digital recall, loss is itself lost
Retromania by the aforementioned Simon Reynolds,8 who as early as 2010 attempted a systematic analysis of our obsession with the recent cultural past

Dating to the late 1990s and early 2000s, it is the aesthetic of the first “internet generation,” a generation that grew up in the 1980s and 1990s amid glittering promises of a better future, but was plagued by the unconscious, subliminal feeling of being trapped

become the ruins of a future glimpsed but never reached: a future in which technology was going to bring us together, improve our quality of life and make us richer, and which has instead tipped us inexorably toward the abyss
the artistic reworking of these symbolic objects reveals a deep-rooted desire for transcendence, the urge to surrender to sensations, a perceptible romantic yearning for the infinite
Piled up all around, the remains of the future lie rotting
For cyberpunks, technology is visceral

Electronic objects suddenly became intimate: keeping us company, preserving memories, shaping places and atmospheres. But computers also generate heat and noise, and are constantly emitting sounds. And at times they glitch, crash, break down

the stripey banding of VHS, the warped effects of the cathode ray tube, the giant pixels of 8bit video games, the endless trails of windows and icons on Windows operating systems … All these elements are spontaneously produced by the limitations of the technology itself, yet are its most recognizable aesthetic

Whatever you find weird, ugly, or nasty about a medium will surely become its signature. CD distortion, the jitteriness of digital video, the crap sound of 8-bit—all these will be cherished and emulated as soon as they can be avoided.
glitches are ghostly
Vaporwave operates in this liminal space, dwelling in the interstices between reality and imagination, inside and out, outer world and inner world
Altered realities, unrealities, surrealities, and derealization all revolve around the idea of how we perceive the world and the possibility of exploring, expanding, and manipulating it.

A passion for transitional spaces, both physical and mental, a sense of solitude, time lag, nostalgia, a yearning for the infinite, a continuous emphasis on the interweaving of memories and sensations: these are all now ubiquitous themes in internet culture

“The reasons for vaporwave being created in the first place are still very much relevant: cynicism about capitalism, sarcastic takes on the unachieved utopias of previous decades, consumerism, escapism, globalization

genre remains relevant because in a sense we are still stuck in the same loop: trapped in a giant shopping mall surrounded by infinite forms of entertainment, disillusioned by politics, melded to technology, obsessed with sensory stimulation, and nostalgic to the core.

In John Koening’s Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, a compendium of invented terms describing complex emotions and sensations, there is a word for this new kind of feeling, namely nostalgia for times that we have never experienced

anemoia, and this is its definition: “Imagine stepping through the frame into a sepia-tinted haze, where you could sit on the side of the road and watch the locals passing by. Who lived and died before any of us arrived here, who sleep in some of the same houses we do, who look up at the same moon, who breathe the same air, feel the same blood in their veins—and live in a completely different world.

Initially a niche phenomenon, in the space of a decade ASMR has become a pillar of internet culture
As well as choosing effective audiovisual triggers, another important thing in these videos is creating a sensation of intimacy
The idea is to generate a feeling of human warmth and connection, to make the viewer feel like they are receiving special attention.

the success of ASMR is one of the many expressions of the so-called “affective turn,”7 which “is associated with a shift toward the importance of the body and its sensations in Western culture as key elements of the individual’s experience of the surrounding reality.”
Far from abandoning the body in favor of purely mental universes, people seem to be interested in using technology for therapeutic, hypnotic, and spiritual purposes

sludge content, a typical example is the TikToks that contain several videos on the same screen.

it is impossible not to see this trend as an attempt to induce a flow state. If all areas of the brain are engaged in focusing on something, we can enter a state of complete absorption that not only feels good but lets us detach from reality for a bit, making us unaware of time passing, our worries, and even our bodily needs.

In a way, excess mental stimulation gives us a glimpse of how we might achieve a sort of ecstasy, an abundant, infinite flow capable of transporting us toward a new self: an amplified, augmented, hypersensitive self.
mood and vibe, the concept of energy is also prevalent in discussions of online cultures
a view based on the belief that the sensations triggered by certain experiences can be recreated and conveyed to others by means of images and sounds
By exchanging visual and auditory stimuli, the hope is to spark a deep connection, even at a distance, ideally enabling people to tune into the same “emotional frequency.”

Today, this vocabulary has diffused beyond any niche group. Yuppies profess to feeling certain energies; New York Times writers divine vibes; venture capitalists do a booming business in moods, pouring money into astrology apps. The occult is for everyone, and so for no one in particular

To consciously create and convey a specific vibe, you need to map it and put together a set of instructions that will enable users to access a specific inner dimension. in the latent space of feelings and sensory experiences, they hunt for an exact intersection of spatial, temporal, and aesthetic coordinates

vibes are not something you just receive; you can also create, reinterpret, select them and come up with new versions. They spread like memes, rippling out through the web, reaching more and more people as the circle widens. The stronger the initial stimulus, the greater the resonance.

title: La azotea
author: Fernanda Trías
description: 'El mundo es esta casa', dice Clara mientras pretende proteger a sus seres queridos de un exterior que le resulta cada vez más amenazante. Clara se atrinchera con su padre y su hija Flor en un apartamento oscuro que irremediablemente se va desmoronando sobre ellos. La azotea se convierte en su último resquicio de libertad. Un pájaro enjaulado es el único testigo del miedo y la resistencia de Clara contra aquellos que intentan destruirla.

description: En estas cinco narraciones intensas y de atmósfera delicada, Guadalupe Nettel nos propone un cruce de caminos entre el mundo animal y el universo humano para hablar de temas tan naturales como la ferocidad de la vida en pareja, la maternidad "cuando es deseada y cuando no lo es", las crisis existenciales de la adolescencia o los lazos inimaginables que pueden establecerse entre dos enamorados. Su mirada proyecta lo subterráneo y lo secreto de sus personajes, lo anómalo, lo inconfesable.

title: Budín del cielo
author: María Luque
description: Rosa es una señora feliz. Jubilada de una de las pasiones de su vida –enseñar matemática a «sus pichoncitos» en el colegio–, vive sola en un departamento lleno de luz que da a la calle, visita con regularidad a su médico de cabecera y se preocupa por su vecina Norma, que tiene unos años menos que ella pero peor salud y bastantes más angustias. Aunque nunca se casó, tuvo varios novios, a quienes le gusta recordar con lujo de detalles. Quizás el gran amor de su vida haya sido, y todavía sea, Sandro: adorablemente vanidosa, a veces se emociona fantaseando con que el cantante también se enamora de ella.
